titel: Exhortations and instructions on the Institute (selections)
warum: The man Ignatius sent across Europe to explain the Exercises and the Institute to the Society itself — the first authorised interpreter.
quelle: Epistolae P. Hieronymi Nadal, MHSI (Madrid 1898–1905); the pre-1930 volumes are US public domain. Latin/Spanish with a working translation.

titel: Practice of Perfection and Christian Virtues (selections)
warum: Three centuries of Jesuit formation read this book; the school of discernment as a daily curriculum.
quelle: Ejercicio de perfección (Seville 1609); early English translations (from 1697) are public domain.

warum: The school distilled to a single motion: the present moment as the sacrament of God's will. Written before the suppression, printed long after — the Favre pattern of transmission.
quelle: L'Abandon à la providence divine, ed. Ramière (1861); E. J. McMahon's English of 1887 is public domain. The attribution is debated and will be stated as such.

warum: The Exercises carried to the other side of the world within a decade of their approval.
quelle: English: H. J. Coleridge, The Life and Letters of St. Francis Xavier, 2 vols. (London 1872; Internet Archive lifelettersofstf01cole / lifelettersofstf02cole, public domain). Four letters carried complete — Cochin 1543, Kagoshima 1549, to Ignatius 1552, Sancian 1552 — cut at their printed openings and datelines, Coleridge's commentary and footnotes omitted. Latin originals: Monumenta Xaveriana (1899–1912), not yet carried.

warum: The order's world reporting: mission, ethnography, martyrdom — annual letters that became a genre.
quelle: Thwaites edition (Cleveland 1896–1901, 73 vols.), French/Latin with English en face; entirely public domain.

warum: Inculturation argued at the court of China: the boldest application of Ignatian adaptability.
quelle: Trigault's Latin (Augsburg 1615), public domain; English would be this site's working translation (Gallagher 1953 in copyright).

titel: Historia natural y moral de las Indias (selections)
warum: A Jesuit empiricism before the word: the New World described by observation against the authorities.
quelle: Seville 1590; Edward Grimston's English of 1604 is public domain.

titel: The centenary emblem book (eleven emblems, with the Dutch mirror)
warum: The order's self-image at one hundred — engraving, epigram and boast in one volume; the very book its critics mocked. Basis of the planned iconographic path.
quelle: Antwerp: Plantin-Moretus 1640; Internet Archive scans imagoprimisaecul00boll (Latin) and afbeeldinghevand00boll (the Dutch Af-Beeldinghe, verses by Adriaen Poirters), both public domain. Shipped: the engraved title and eleven emblems — one from each of the six books plus three deepenings — as page images with the epigrams transcribed distich by distich, working translations, and each emblem's Dutch mirror page with Poirters's rhymed gloss. The volume's remaining ~110 emblems wait their turn; the iconographic reading path runs through the spine of seven.

warum: Conscience from inside the order against the witch trials: the confessor of the condemned turns witness against the procedure.
quelle: Latin transcribed by eye from the page images of the anonymous first printing (Rinteln: Petrus Lucius, 1631; Internet Archive per_witchcraft-in-europe-and-america_spee-friedrich-von_1631_911, public domain). Shipped complete: Dubium I (the opening question) and Dubium LI (the numbered summa of the trials, pp. 378–392), with this site's working translation (CC0). The torture dubia are the named next step.

warum: The same conscience as poetry: the counter-voice singing.
quelle: German transcribed by eye from the page images of the Cologne print of 1654 (Internet Archive trutz-nachtigall-oder-geistlichs-poetisc, public domain; first published posthumously 1649). Shipped: two celebrated poems complete — the Oelberg lament and the spring 'Liebgesang der Gesponss Jesu' — with this site's working prose translation (CC0). The rest of the ~50 poems wait their turn.

titel: The forged 'secret instructions' of the Society
warum: A forgery that forced a debate — carried as the debate, not as truth: the apparatus's Turk, with the refutations beside it.
quelle: Kraków 1614 (Zahorowski). Carried from the bilingual printing of 1857: W. C. Brownlee, Secret Instructions of the Jesuits (New York, American and Foreign Christian Union; Internet Archive instructiosecret00browrich, public domain) — Latin and English on facing pages, chapter and article numbering as the alignment grid; OCR repaired against the page images, all 145 articles bilingual.

warum: The most brilliant attack the Society ever received: casuistry examined by a genius with a grudge and a printing press.
quelle: M'Crie's translation of 1856 (Robert Carter & Brothers), via Project Gutenberg #73959, public domain; Letters V, VII and X complete. French original: the Vallée transcription on fr.wikisource — not yet carried.

titel: Dominus ac Redemptor — the brief of suppression
warum: The corpus's intended closing text: the document that dissolved the old Society. The apparatus ends, deliberately, in 1773.
quelle: Latin after Augustin Theiner, Clementis XIV. Pont. Max. Epistolae et Brevia (Paris, 1852), doc. CCCXVII, whose paragraph numbering (1–41) is carried as the citation grid; Internet Archive clementisxivpon00clemgoog, public domain, OCR emended against the page images. English: this site's unofficial working translation, made directly from the Latin — no full public-domain English translation exists (Nicolini 1854 translates only the restoration brief of 1814).
